subject: BAM file being sorted by featureCounts despite `--donotsort` [v1.5.3]

messages.author: ab6dbc67ee8c01b4
messages.subject: BAM file being sorted by featureCounts despite `--donotsort` [v1.5.3]
parts:
Hello, 

I'm trying to use featureCounts to count reads in 1-kbp bins tiling the entire genome for some downstream CNV calling. The input data are paired-end BAM files from whole genome sequencing, so they're quite large (200+ GB). Accordingly, I would prefer to avoid re-sorting the BAM files, as it adds significant overhead in terms of time and disk usage. I would be okay with the trade-off of considering paired reads individually. 

However, when I added the --donotsort option, I noticed that featureCounts is still generating a sorted BAM file (i.e. *.sam.fixbam). Is this expected? I'm using featureCounts v1.5.3.  Here's the command I'm running: 

featureCounts -a windows.1000.saf -F SAF -o output.read_counts.ws_1000.tsv --donotsort -O --largestOverlap --ignoreDup -s 0 -T 12 input.bam

Cheers,
Bruno

messages.author: bce99ba71cd48eea
messages.subject: Re: BAM file being sorted by featureCounts despite `--donotsort` [v1.5.3]
parts:
Hi Bruno,

I tested the "--donotsort" option and it worked appropriately.

The ".fixbam" file you've seen in the directory is the temporary BAM file for fixing the format of your input BAM file; it wasn't for sorting. As I know, featureCounts needs to fix the BAM files from STAR and Picard because an alignment record in these BAM files can go into two or even more BAM blocks (each ~ 64kb after decompression).

Cheers,
Yang
